newsitem.title: USA: New York City to sell $1.6 bln of notes on Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: New York City to sell $1.6 bln of notes on Oct 1.

text.p: New York City plans to sell $1.6 billion of revenue anticipation notes by competitive bid on October 1, said a city official on Friday.

The city, one of the biggest issuers in the municipal debt market, also plans to sell approximately $500 million of general obligation bonds to raise new money at the end of October, the city official said.

The timing of both sales has been shifted somewhat, with the note sale slightly delayed. In late August, New York City had said it expected to sell the notes in mid- to late-September. The bond sale had been planned for November.
No explanation for the adjustments in the timing of the city's debt offerings was immediately available.
The bond issue, which will be sold through the city's syndicate by negotiation, might be raised to include $250 to $500 million of refunding bonds.
"The typical range is $750 million to $1 billion," the city official said, explaining that is how big New York City's bond sales for this period tend to run.
And New York City might sell $50 to $100 million of taxable issues at the same time, which would be sold by competition.

The revenue anticipation notes to be sold on October 1 will be comprised of two different maturities, with as much as $550 million maturing at the end of March, and as much as $1.25 billion expiring at the end of June.

Because New York state has a history of failing to approve its budgets, due on April 1, on time, the city official said that to avoid any problems, New York City will back the June portion of the notes with a letter of credit.
This is a strategy the city has used in the past, though it increases its borrowing costs.
